evidence: techtest.org, 21 April 2024, measured nine AA alkaline cells. It lists Varta at EUR 0.40 and dm Paradies at EUR 0.19 per cell, and ranks Paradies 1st at both 0.1 A and 0.4 A, and Varta 9th at both. The article puts the 0.1 A range at 2,226 to 2,477 mAh. TECHBOOK, 12 August 2023, measured a Varta Longlife at EUR 0.63 and 0.903 V after ten hours, also below the cheaper cells it tested, and did not test Paradies.
differences: One site, a small sample and one date. Which Varta line techtest used isn't clear from the name it gives, and Varta sells several. No test here covers shelf life or leakage, and Varta's own ranges differ.
why: In this test the cheaper cell gave the most capacity and the dearer one the least, so the price did not track the result.
